title: Boundary Assurance: Forensic Seal API, Retention Policies, and Automated Audit Bundles for Dedicated Tenants
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a single, auditable 'forensic seal' artifact and a small HTTP RPC surface that (1) collects residency and tenant-boundary evidence from dedicated nodes, (2) packages signed audit bundles with retention metadata, and (3) exposes a queryable attestation API for downstream reporting and auditor ingestion. This ticket scopes the API contract, retention model, packaging format, signing strategy, and an initial automation worker to produce nightly bundles for all Dedicated tenants.

Deliverables:
- Forensic Seal API (POST /v1/tenants/:id/attestations, GET /v1/tenants/:id/attestations/:bundle_id) with RBAC checks and signed manifests.
- Evidence bundle format: gzipped tarball containing node-metadata.json, log-sample.jsonl, network-routing-snapshot.json, kms-key-refs.txt, and a signed manifest (manifest.json + manifest.sig).
- Retention controls: default TTL=365 days, configurable per-tenant (min 30 days, max 1825 days), support for immediate purge request and legal_hold flag to prevent deletion.
- Signing: sign manifests server-side using Redwood platform signing key; allow optional tenant-supplied KMS wrapping for manifests (KMS key id reference stored in tenant config).
- Automation: nightly worker that triggers per-tenant bundle generation, stores bundles in S3 with lifecycle rules, and writes attestation metadata to the attestation DB.
- Observability: console dashboard card showing last successful bundle, time-to-generate, bundle size, and retention expiry.
- Audit endpoints for exports: CSV/NDJSON listing of bundles and retention states for a given date range.

Design decisions & trade-offs considered:
- Bundle vs. streaming evidence: a bundle provides a stable snapshot for auditors and is easier to sign and version; streaming would reduce latency but complicates verification and increases storage churn. We chose nightly bundles as a pragmatic first step.
- Where to store artifacts: S3 with per-tenant prefixes + server-side KMS encryption is cheapest and reliable. We accept the dependence on object storage lifecycle semantics.
- Signing model: server signing provides strong non-repudiation for platform attestations; optional tenant KMS integration is supported but adds complexity to key rotation flows and failure modes.
- Retention enforcement: lifecycle policies on S3 + a retention-indexing service that prevents accidental deletion when legal_hold=true. This duplicates some semantics but gives us a fast enforcement path.

API sketch (open contract):
- POST /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/attestations?force=false -> 202 Accepted + job_id (triggers immediate bundle generation if force=true, otherwise scheduled).
- GET /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/attestations -> list bundles with metadata (bundle_id, created_at, expiration_at, size_bytes, signature_present).
- GET /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/attestations/:bundle_id -> presigned S3 URL + manifest.
- DELETE /v1/tenants/:tenant_id/attestations/:bundle_id -> soft-delete request (respects legal_hold), returns 204 or 403 if blocked.

Acceptance criteria:
- A nightly worker produces a valid signed bundle for 100% of dedicated tenants in staging.
- The bundle can be downloaded and verified (manifest.sig verifies against Redwood signing key).
- Retention TTL is enforced and visible in console for a sample tenant; manual purge path works and respects legal_hold.
- Endpoint RBAC: only tenant admins and Redwood compliance role can trigger and fetch attestations.

Implementation notes & tasks:
- Schema: attestation metadata table (flat columns: bundle_id, tenant_id, created_at, expires_at, s3_key, size_bytes, signature_key_id, kms_wrapped boolean).
- Worker: reuse existing job-queue infra; new step to collect node snapshots, compress, sign, upload, and persist metadata.
- RBAC: wire to platform IAM, add new permission scope 'attestations:read' and 'attestations:write'.
- UI: small Console card; link to diagnostics and ability to change per-tenant retention TTL.
- Security: key rotation playbook for platform signing key; on rotation create cross-signed epoch manifests.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we need to include sampling of encrypted request payloads or is metadata sufficient? (PM prefers metadata-only to avoid PII exposure.)
- Should we support ad-hoc bundle generation by 3rd-party auditors? (treat as follow-up after controlled access is validated)
- Legal_hold semantics across dedicated->private migrations (requires coordination with migrations team).

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: complete API and bundle format proto, unit tests, and DB schema.
- Week 2: implement worker + S3 lifecycle, end-to-end tests in staging.
- Week 3: stealth deploy for 5 pilot tenants, gather feedback and verify SLAs.
- Week 4: platform-wide roll with console card and runbook published.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Generation success rate >= 99% per night.
- Bundle generation p95 latency < 10 minutes for 95% tenants.
- Alert on repeated failures for the same tenant (3 failed nights) to oncall.

Security & Compliance notes:
- Security reviewed data flows with Security team 2025-02-14 (see meeting notes in confluence).
- Platform signing key material stored in HSM; signing operation performed in a hardened signing service with strict ACLs.
- All bundles encrypted at rest with server-side KMS; optional tenant-supplied KMS reference stored as ID only (no plaintext keys).
